title: Evidence-Based Longevity Supplements - Healthpath
abstract:
PQQ stands out for its unique ability to stimulate the creation of new mitochondria, a process called mitochondrial biogenesis. Studies show that PQQ stimulates the generation of new mitochondria, enhance cellular energy metabolism, and slow down the decline of mitochondrial function associated with ageing.  
This powerful compound also functions as an antioxidant, neutralising free radicals and reducing cellular oxidative damage. The combination of increased mitochondrial numbers and reduced oxidative stress makes PQQ a valuable addition to any longevity-focused supplement regimen.  
**👉 Recommended product:** [PQQ](https://my.healthpath.com/products/mito-pqq-60s/22678/?referral=15)  
Resveratrol, a polyphenol found in red wine and grapes, has been extensively studied for its longevity-promoting properties. Research published in *Nature Cell Biology* established that mice treated with sirtuin-activating compounds (STACs) such as resveratrol have improved organ function, physical endurance, disease resistance and longevity.  
The compound works by allosterically activating SIRT1, effectively mimicking some benefits of caloric restriction without reducing food intake. Studies across multiple species demonstrate that resveratrol can extend lifespan and improve healthspan by enhancing mitochondrial function, reducing inflammation, and supporting metabolic health.
While resveratrol has relatively low bioavailability, research continues to demonstrate its beneficial effects on cardiovascular health, cognitive function, and metabolic disorders.  
**👉 Recommended product:** [Resveratrol](https://my.healthpath.com/products/resveratrol-max-60s/20338/?referral=15)  
Taurine, a sulfur-containing amino acid, has emerged as a powerful SIRT1 activator with remarkable anti-aging properties. Groundbreaking research published in *Science* revealed that taurine supplementation extended both median and maximum lifespans in multiple species including worms, rodents, and non-human primates.  
Molecular docking studies confirm that taurine activates SIRT1 via direct interaction with the protein, though interestingly through a different binding site than resveratrol. Human epidemiological data shows that taurine levels naturally decline with aging, and maintaining adequate levels appears crucial for healthy longevity.  
The comprehensive benefits of taurine include enhanced mitochondrial function, reduced oxidative stress, improved cardiovascular health, and activation of longevity pathways. Studies demonstrate that taurine can reduce inflammation, improve insulin sensitivity, and support overall metabolic health.  
**👉 Recommended product:** [Taurine](https://my.healthpath.com/products/taurine-1000mg-100s/5959/?referral=15)
Astaxanthin, a powerful carotenoid pigment, has gained recognition as a geroprotective compound with multiple longevity benefits. Research indicates that astaxanthin can modulate Nrf2, FOXO3, Sirt1, and Klotho proteins that are linked to longevity.  
This remarkable antioxidant crosses the blood-brain barrier and has shown particular promise in protecting against neurodegenerative diseases and supporting cognitive function. Studies demonstrate that astaxanthin enhances SIRT1 expression and activity, contributing to improved mitochondrial function and reduced oxidative stress.  
Clinical research has shown astaxanthin’s ability to protect cardiovascular health, support cognitive function, and combat age-related oxidative damage throughout the body.  
**👉 Recommended product:** [Astaxanthin](https://my.healthpath.com/products/astaxanthin-7mg-120s/23608/?referral=15)  
Dihydroberberine represents a highly bioavailable form of berberine with enhanced effectiveness. Research published in *Diabetes* demonstrates that dihydroberberine inhibits mitochondrial respiratory complex I, activating AMPK and improving insulin action.  
Studies show dihydroberberine is up to 5 times more bioavailable than regular berberine and lasts twice as long in the system. This improved pharmacokinetics translates to better metabolic benefits with lower doses.
